title: Dreams Money Can Buy
summary:
Dreams Money Can Buy
The United States of America has a new president. The "Chief Executive" position is to be passed over to Senator Barack Obama in January 2009 and it seems that the new team in the White House has their work cut out for them. The next year will likely prove to be trying for the American people for a variety of reasons both economic and social.

children.title: US Gasoline Prices
children.summary: The ailing economy has created challenges for many industries, but energy related businesses have tended to fare better than most. Oil companies have reported another quarter of strong profits (helped largely by high oil prices) and tanker companies have enjoyed record earnings so far in 2008.

children.title: New Energy for America
children.summary: Although this year's presidential election was largely determined by the poor management of the economy, energy issues played a key role. The President-elect has some ideas for tackling energy issues.

children.summary: The first action is an expected enactment of a Windfall Profits Tax on oil companies as a way to pass a "rebate" check to consumers. A policy such as this would ostensibly deter companies from making investments to increase supply as the upside economic potential is arbitrarily capped, further deepening our dependence on foreign oil.

children.summary: Clean coal technology is being heralded as a panacea for greenhouse gas emissions and a way to create jobs. Developing the technology makes sense as coal is a plentiful natural resource in America, however developing new jobs could potentially mean cannibalizing other jobs in the energy sector as a result.
